numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For a tz-naive Timestamp plus or minus a timedelta64 ndarray, the raw self.asm8 +/- other wraps silently, both when numpy promotes to the finer unit and in the addition itself, returning an incorrect datetime64 array.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The operation should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime when the result is out of bounds, matching the tz-aware branch of the same method. The cast to the finer unit should also raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta when the coarser operand has to be cast.
trigger_conditions: operand is a numpy timedelta64 ndarray (is_array branch of _Timestamp.__add__/__sub__)
numpy promotes the operands to the finer of the two units (e.g. Timestamp in 's' plus m8[ns] array), which wraps
the addition itself overflows int64 nanoseconds (e.g. 9*10**18 m8[ns] added to 2000-01-01)

numerical_characteristics.dtype: m8[ns] / m8[s] / m8[us] / int64 (timedelta64 ndarray operands; int64 view misread for big-endian m8)
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Timestamp at 2500-01-01 cast to ns overflows; other operand value 2**62 in m8[s] overflows to 4611686018427387904 seconds when cast to timedelta64[ns]; year/month and sub-nanosecond units excluded from the fix
category_specific_evidence: Overflow/wrap in promotion: ts=Timestamp('2500-01-01').as_unit('s') plus np.array([1], dtype='m8[ns]') previously wrapped on numpy's promotion to the finer unit; now raises OutOfBoundsDatetime 'Cannot cast 2500-01-01 00:00:00 to unit=ns without overflow' (GH#66552)
Reverse case: ts=Timestamp('2000-01-01').as_unit('ns') with np.array([2**62], dtype='m8[s]') now raises OutOfBoundsTimedelta 'Cannot convert 4611686018427387904 seconds to timedelta64'
Addition itself wrapped: the raw asm8 +/- other path wrapped in the addition, now routed through add_overflowsafe
Adjacent bug: ts.as_unit('s') + np.array([1], '>m8[s]') returned year 2283416254 due to int64 view misreading non-native byteorder buffer; a big-endian m8 test was added
Verification: exact Python-int oracle over 4 Timestamp resolutions x 8 timedelta64 units x 400 magnitudes x add/sub gave 0 mismatches
Preserved numpy behaviors: m8[Y]/m8[M] and sub-nanosecond units fall through to numpy (numpy raises UFuncTypeError for Y/M); generic m8 read in other operand's unit; 0-dim input returns numpy scalar
Performance cost: 1M-element Timestamp + m8[us] went 1.3 ms -> 14.9 ms
reproduction_risks: Big-endian m8 buffers require byteorder handling; viewing as int64 misreads them
Generic m8 arrays take the other operand's unit, so the reproduction must use a unit-bearing timedelta when testing promotion
m8[Y]/m8[M] and sub-ns units bypass the fix and raise via numpy, not OutOfBoundsDatetime
Overflow thresholds depend on Timestamp resolution; the 2500-01-01 example is only overflowing at ns
Tz-aware branch is a separate path and is not covered by this fix
